inheritanceRule: Every omitted field inherits the resolved parent class value.

profiles.name: Armored Battlemage

evidence.reason: The arcane pool enhances armour and a full armour-training progression replaces offensive spell-combat improvements.

profiles.playerSummary: A heavily armoured Magus who channels arcane-pool power into armour instead of weapons.
profiles.tradeoff: Spell combat is lost entirely, substantially weakening the normal cast-and-strike action economy.

profiles.name: Hexcrafter

evidence.reason: Witch hexes and curse spells make lasting magical hindrance the archetype’s defining addition.

profiles.playerSummary: A Magus who integrates Witch hexes and curse magic into an already aggressive spell-and-weapon chassis.
profiles.tradeoff: Several Magus arcana choices are redirected into hexes, increasing option and resource complexity.

profiles.name: Eldritch Scion

constraints.summary: One bloodrager bloodline determines bonus spells and bloodline powers.

evidence.reason: The Magus becomes a spontaneous Charisma caster tied to a bloodrager bloodline.

profiles.playerSummary: A spontaneous Charisma-based Magus whose arcane pool and combat magic awaken through a bloodrager bloodline.
profiles.tradeoff: Spell combat is delayed and restricted by mystical focus, and the bloodline is a permanent build commitment.

profiles.name: Burglar

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The archetype explicitly specialises in breaking in, bypassing traps and diverting attention.

evidence.reason: Trap handling and getaway distraction reinforce the explicit burglary vocation.

profiles.playerSummary: A professional burglar specialised in careful trap work, covert entry and distracting pursuit during an escape.
profiles.tradeoff: Trap sense and uncanny dodge are replaced by situational infiltration techniques.

profiles.name: Scout

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The archetype explicitly fights through movement, charging and mobile reconnaissance-style attacks.

evidence.reason: Charge and movement directly enable sneak attack, making mobility central to offence.

profiles.playerSummary: A mobile Rogue who creates sneak-attack openings by charging or moving across the battlefield.
profiles.tradeoff: Uncanny dodge is lost, and peak offence depends on having room and actions to move.

profiles.name: Thug

evidence.reason: Demoralisation lasts longer and sneak attack can impose sickened instead of extra damage.

profiles.playerSummary: An intimidating Rogue who prolongs fear and trades some sneak-attack damage for brutal debilitating blows.
profiles.tradeoff: Trapfinding and trap sense are reduced for a style that depends on fear and vulnerable targets.

profiles.name: Eldritch Scrapper

evidence.reason: Temporary combat feats and bloodline weapon proficiency add a genuine martial route.

profiles.playerSummary: A Sorcerer who trades early bloodline powers for flexible combat feats and weapons associated with the bloodline.
profiles.tradeoff: It remains a low-BAB caster and must understand the combat-feat tree to use its flexibility well.

profiles.name: Seeker

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The archetype explicitly searches out magical secrets, disables devices and studies hidden lore.

evidence.reason: Trapfinding and Disable Device expertise add a practical exploration role absent from the base Sorcerer.

profiles.playerSummary: A Sorcerer seeker who investigates magical secrets, handles traps and pushes bloodline magic beyond ordinary limits.
profiles.tradeoff: Several bloodline powers are delayed or replaced by a specialised exploration package.

profiles.name: Tattooed Sorcerer

constraints.summary: A familiar is embodied in a magical tattoo and replaces the normal 1st-level bloodline power.

evidence.reason: A tattoo familiar becomes a persistent magical companion with unusual concealment.

profiles.playerSummary: A Sorcerer whose bloodline manifests through magical tattoos and a familiar that can retreat into the skin.
profiles.tradeoff: The 1st-level bloodline power is lost and much of the archetype’s identity is tied to visible tattoos and one familiar.

profiles.name: Scroll Scholar

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The archetype explicitly develops multiple fields of scholarship and language and identification expertise.

evidence.reason: Scaling Knowledge specialities support the explicit scholarly identity without changing the Wizard’s already-core knowledge role.

profiles.playerSummary: A Wizard scholar who accumulates specialised fields of knowledge, reads obscure texts and produces sudden flashes of insight.
profiles.tradeoff: The arcane school’s normal power progression is reduced for broadly applicable but less dramatic scholarship.
